title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 11.

questions.question: Where did all Israel gather to anoint David king?
questions.explanation: All Israel gathered themselves to David unto Hebron and anointed him king there, as stated in 1 Chronicles 11:1-3.

questions.question: Who was king of Israel before David, according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: The text refers to Saul as king before David, specifically in 1 Chronicles 11:2.

questions.question: What was the reason given by the people for coming to David at Hebron?
options: We are thy bone and thy flesh
questions.correctAnswer: We are thy bone and thy flesh
questions.explanation: The people said, 'Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh,' indicating their close kinship and support, as in 1 Chronicles 11:1.

questions.question: What city did David and all Israel go to after Hebron?
questions.explanation: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, which was also called Jebus, as noted in 1 Chronicles 11:4.

questions.question: True or False: The inhabitants of Jebus welcomed David to their city.
questions.explanation: The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, 'Thou shalt not come hither,' indicating they did not welcome him, as in 1 Chronicles 11:5.

questions.question: Who was the first to strike the Jebusites and become chief and captain?
questions.explanation: David said whoever smote the Jebusites first would be chief; Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first and was chief, from 1 Chronicles 11:6.

questions.question: True or False: David lived in the castle after taking the city, which then was called the city of David.
questions.explanation: David dwelt in the castle, and it was therefore called the city of David, as stated in 1 Chronicles 11:7.

questions.question: Who repaired the rest of the city after David built it around Millo?
questions.explanation: Joab repaired the rest of the city after David built it around Millo, according to 1 Chronicles 11:8.

questions.question: What is the reason given for David waxing greater and greater?
options: The LORD of hosts was with him
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD of hosts was with him
questions.explanation: David waxed greater and greater because the LORD of hosts was with him, as stated in 1 Chronicles 11:9.

questions.question: Who was the chief of the captains among David's mighty men, known for slaying three hundred at one time?
questions.explanation: Jashobeam, an Hachmonite, was the chief of the captains and lifted his spear against three hundred slain at one time, per 1 Chronicles 11:11.

questions.question: True or False: Eleazar the son of Dodo was one of the three mighties of David.
questions.explanation: Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, was one of the three mighties, as stated in 1 Chronicles 11:12.

questions.question: What did the Philistines gather together to do at Pasdammim?
questions.explanation: The Philistines were gathered together to battle at Pasdammim, as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 11:13.

questions.question: What was the state of the people before the Philistines at the parcel of ground full of barley?
questions.explanation: The people fled before the Philistines, but the three mighties set themselves in the midst and delivered the parcel, according to 1 Chronicles 11:13-14.

questions.question: Where did three of the thirty captains go down to David?
questions.explanation: Three of the thirty captains went down to David into the cave of Adullam, as per 1 Chronicles 11:15.

questions.question: True or False: David was in the hold while the Philistines' garrison was at Bethlehem.
questions.explanation: David was then in the hold, and the Philistines' garrison was then at Bethlehem, according to 1 Chronicles 11:16.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did David long for while he was in the hold, according to 1 Chronicles 11?
options: Water from the well of Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: Water from the well of Bethlehem
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:17 states that David longed for a drink of water from the well of Bethlehem, which was at the gate.

questions.question: How did David respond when the three mighty men brought him water from Bethlehem's well?
options: He poured it out as an offering to the LORD
He shared it with his men
questions.correctAnswer: He poured it out as an offering to the LORD
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 11:18, David did not drink the water but poured it out to the LORD, showing his reverence and respect for the risk the men took.

questions.question: Why did David refuse to drink the water brought by the three mightiest men?
options: He did not want to drink the blood of the men who risked their lives
He wanted to save it for later
questions.correctAnswer: He did not want to drink the blood of the men who risked their lives
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:19 explains that David said it was forbidden for him to drink the water because it represented the blood of the men who risked their lives to get it.

questions.question: Who was the chief of the three mighty men that brought water to David and was also the brother of Joab?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:20 identifies Abishai, Joab's brother, as the chief of the three mighty men who brought water to David.

questions.question: True or False: Abishai attained to the first three mighty men according to 1 Chronicles 11.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:21 states that although Abishai was more honorable than the other two and was their captain, he did not attain to the first three mighty men.

questions.question: Which mighty man slew two lion-like men of Moab and a lion in a pit on a snowy day?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:22 describes Benaiah's valorous acts including slaying two lion-like men of Moab and a lion in a pit on a snowy day.

questions.question: How did Benaiah kill the Egyptian man of great stature, and what was notable about the weapon involved?
options: He used his own spear to kill the Egyptian
He plucked the Egyptian's spear, which was like a weaver's beam, and killed him with it
He killed him with a sword given by David
He trapped him in a pit and killed him there
questions.correctAnswer: He plucked the Egyptian's spear, which was like a weaver's beam, and killed him with it
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:23 explains that Benaiah took the spear from the Egyptian, described as being like a weaver's beam, and killed him with his own weapon.

questions.question: What position did David assign to Benaiah after recognizing his honors among the thirty mighty men?
options: Chief of the three mighty men
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:25 states that David set Benaiah over his guard after acknowledging his honorable status among the thirty mighty men.

questions.question: Which of the following names is NOT listed as one of the valiant men of David's armies in 1 Chronicles 11?
questions.explanation: Verses 26-47 list many valiant men, including Asahel, Elhanan, and Shammoth, but Goliath is not included as one of David's men.

questions.question: True or False: David’s refusal to drink the water brought by his men teaches us about humility and reverence for sacrifice.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:18-19 show David's humility and reverence by pouring out the water as an offering rather than drinking what was risked for him, illustrating respect for sacrifice.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 11:19 promise will happen if one honors the sacrifices of others, as David did with the water?
options: God will forbid them to prosper
They will be blessed and honored by God
They will be punished for pride
questions.correctAnswer: They will be blessed and honored by God
questions.explanation: David's act of not drinking the water out of respect for the lives risked (verse 19) demonstrates a principle that honoring sacrifice leads to God's blessing and honor, as implied by his actions and God's favor shown in earlier verses.

questions.question: How does the story of the three mighty men bringing water to David (verses 15-19) teach about faith and trust in God during adversity?
options: It shows that relying on human strength alone is enough
It emphasizes risking life with faith that God will protect and deliver
It warns against taking risks in battle
It suggests waiting passively for God’s intervention
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes risking life with faith that God will protect and deliver
questions.explanation: Verses 15-19 describe the bravery of the men breaking through enemy lines to get water, trusting God’s protection, showing faith and courage in adversity.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 11, what virtue is demonstrated by David's act of pouring out the water instead of drinking it?
questions.explanation: David’s refusal to drink the water, pouring it out as an offering, demonstrates humility and respect for the sacrifice of the men, as shown in verses 18-19.

questions.question: True or False: Benaiah was honored among the thirty mighty men but did not reach the status of the first three mighty men.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:25 clearly states that Benaiah was honorable among the thirty but did not attain to the first three mighty men.

questions.question: Which lesson from 1 Chronicles 11:22-25 best helps a believer facing challenges requiring courage and faith?
options: Bravery and faith lead to recognition and responsibility
Rely on others to fight your battles
questions.correctAnswer: Bravery and faith lead to recognition and responsibility
questions.explanation: Benaiah’s courageous acts (verses 22-24) and subsequent appointment over the guard (verse 25) teach that faith and bravery bring honor and responsibility.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 11.

questions.question: Who was the armourbearer of Joab, son of Zeruiah, mentioned among David's mighty men?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:39 identifies Naharai the Berothite as the armourbearer of Joab son of Zeruiah.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT listed as one of the mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11:33-47?
questions.explanation: Eleazar the Ahohite is mentioned earlier in 1 Chronicles 11:12, not in the list from verses 33-47.

questions.question: What role did Adina son of Shiza hold among the mighty men?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:42 states Adina son of Shiza was a captain of the Reubenites.

questions.question: Which geographic designation is shared by Ira and Gareb in the list of David's mighty men?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:40 names Ira and Gareb both as Ithrites.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 11, which mighty man was noted for slaying two lionlike men of Moab and a lion in a pit on a snowy day?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:22 describes Benaiah's deeds including slaying two lionlike men of Moab and a lion in a pit.

questions.question: What was David's reaction after the three mighty men brought him water from the well of Bethlehem?
options: He drank it as a sign of victory
He poured it out as an offering to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He poured it out as an offering to the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:18-19 explain David poured out the water to the LORD, refusing to drink it because it was brought at great risk.

questions.question: Which literary device is exemplified by the detailed listing of David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11:10-47?
questions.explanation: The chapter uses inclusio by framing David’s reign with the gathering of his mighty men, emphasizing their importance throughout the narrative (1 Chronicles 11:10-47).

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated 'mighty men' in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'Gibborim' used here means 'mighty men' or 'valiant warriors,' highlighting their strength and valor (1 Chronicles 11:10).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage does the anointing of David as king in 1 Chronicles 11:3 directly connect with?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:3 references David's anointing as king, which is originally recorded in 1 Samuel 16, where Samuel anoints David.

questions.question: What historical significance does the naming of 'the city of David' in 1 Chronicles 11:7 hold?
options: It signifies David's conquest and establishment of Jerusalem as his capital
It marks the division of Israel into two kingdoms
It commemorates the building of the Temple
It records the exile of the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies David's conquest and establishment of Jerusalem as his capital
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:7 shows David dwelling in the castle, which led to the city being called 'the city of David,' marking Jerusalem's establishment as his capital.

questions.question: Which mighty man was noted for lifting up his spear against three hundred men at one time, as recorded in this chapter?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:11 identifies Jashobeam as the chief of captains who killed three hundred men at one time.

questions.question: True or False: David’s mighty men only included warriors from Judah and Benjamin tribes.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:41-46 lists mighty men from various tribes including Reubenites, Moabites, and others, showing diversity beyond Judah and Benjamin.

questions.question: Which passage in the New Testament echoes the theme of faithful warriors in 1 Chronicles 11 by emphasizing spiritual battle and steadfastness?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 6:10-18 speaks of putting on the 'whole armor of God,' reflecting spiritual steadfastness similar to David’s mighty men’s valor in 1 Chronicles 11.

questions.question: Who was the brother of Joab that was chief of the three mighty men but did not attain to the first three, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:20-21 explains Abishai, Joab’s brother, was chief of the three mighty men but did not reach the top three.

questions.question: True or False: David made a covenant with the elders of Israel before the LORD in Hebron before being anointed king over Israel.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:3 states that David made a covenant with the elders of Israel in Hebron before the LORD and was anointed king.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's sovereignty and human leadership is demonstrated when Israel anointed David king according to the word of the LORD by Samuel?
options: God ordains human rulers as part of His divine plan
Human kingship is purely a human decision without divine involvement
Samuel acted independently of God's will in anointing David
David seized the throne by force without any covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains human rulers as part of His divine plan
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 11:3 shows that David was anointed king according to the word of the LORD by Samuel, indicating that God sovereignly appoints leaders.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 11:5, how does David's taking of the castle of Zion illustrate the theological theme of God's empowerment in conquest?
options: David's victory was assured by God's presence despite opposition
David conquered Zion by his own military might alone
The Jebusites willingly surrendered without resistance
David negotiated a peace treaty with the inhabitants
questions.correctAnswer: David's victory was assured by God's presence despite opposition
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows the Jebusites' defiance, yet David took the castle, indicating God's empowering presence in his conquest.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly revealed by the statement in 1 Chronicles 11:9 that 'the LORD of hosts was with him' as David waxed greater and greater?
options: God's omnipotence and faithfulness to His promises
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence and faithfulness to His promises
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the LORD of hosts was with him' in verse 9 highlights God's almighty power and faithfulness in supporting David's reign.

questions.question: What theological insight about sanctification and faithfulness is taught by David's refusal to drink the water brought by his three mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11:18-19?
options: David honored the risk his men took by not profaning their sacrifice
David was thirsty and drank the water eagerly
David disregarded the bravery of his men
David punished the men for risking their lives
questions.correctAnswer: David honored the risk his men took by not profaning their sacrifice
questions.explanation: Verses 18-19 show David's refusal to drink the water to avoid treating their sacrifice lightly, reflecting sanctification and respect for God’s gift.

questions.question: How does the mention of Benaiah's exploits in 1 Chronicles 11:22-23 illustrate the doctrine of divine providence in the lives of God's servants?
options: God providentially equips and protects His people in their battles
Benaiah's victories were purely due to his own strength
God was unaware of Benaiah's acts
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially equips and protects His people in their battles
questions.explanation: Benaiah’s feats in verses 22-23 demonstrate God's providential care empowering His servants for significant deeds.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 1-3 and 9 convey about God's role in establishing David's kingship and blessing his reign?
options: God both appoints and sustains His chosen king with His presence
David became king through human politics alone
God abandoned David after his anointing
David's reign prospered despite God's absence
questions.correctAnswer: God both appoints and sustains His chosen king with His presence
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 show God's appointment of David as king, while verse 9 confirms God's presence empowering David’s increasing success.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 11:6 and 11:20, what doctrine can be drawn about leadership qualities among God's mighty men?
options: Courage and valor in battle are marks of God-ordained leadership
Leadership is based on birthright only
Leaders avoid conflict to preserve themselves
Leadership is unrelated to spiritual or physical courage
questions.correctAnswer: Courage and valor in battle are marks of God-ordained leadership
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows Joab becoming captain by courageously engaging first, and verse 20 shows Abishai’s valor, both highlighting God’s valuing of bravery in leaders.

questions.question: What does the gathering of all Israel to David in Hebron in 1 Chronicles 11:1-2 reveal about the unity of God's people under His chosen king?
options: God's people are united in recognizing His anointed ruler
Israel was divided and rejected David
David ruled only a small faction
God's people preferred Saul over David
questions.correctAnswer: God's people are united in recognizing His anointed ruler
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 depict Israel gathering and affirming David as 'bone and flesh,' showing unity under God’s chosen king.

questions.question: How does the narrative of David's conquest of Jerusalem (verses 4-7) foreshadow Christ's eternal kingship?
options: David’s establishing a city of refuge and rule prefigures Christ’s eternal kingdom
David's conquest was limited and temporary
questions.correctAnswer: David’s establishing a city of refuge and rule prefigures Christ’s eternal kingdom
questions.explanation: Verses 4-7 describe David’s establishment of Jerusalem, the 'city of David,' foreshadowing Christ’s eternal reign and the spiritual kingdom He inaugurates.

questions.question: What apologetic response does 1 Chronicles 11:10-11 provide against the claim that David’s mighty men were mere exaggerations in Scripture?
options: The detailed naming and specific feats of mighty men confirm historical reliability
The names are anonymous and lack detail
The Scripture exaggerates for literary effect only
questions.correctAnswer: The detailed naming and specific feats of mighty men confirm historical reliability
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 give named individuals and their exploits, supporting Scripture’s historical accuracy against sceptics.

questions.question: What theological insight about human frailty and God's sustaining power can be drawn from the contrast between the Philistines' encampment and David's hold in verses 15-16?
options: Though David was in a vulnerable position, God sustained him amidst enemies
David was completely safe and untouched by conflict
The Philistines were powerless and insignificant
questions.correctAnswer: Though David was in a vulnerable position, God sustained him amidst enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 15-16 show David in a hold surrounded by enemies, highlighting human vulnerability but implying God's sustaining presence.

questions.question: What doctrine of sanctification is underscored by David’s act of pouring out the water to the LORD rather than drinking it in 1 Chronicles 11:19?
options: Respecting the cost of sacrifice and refusing to partake in bloodshed profanely
Drinking the water would have been a holy act
David was indifferent to the sacrifice of his men
The water had no symbolic value
questions.correctAnswer: Respecting the cost of sacrifice and refusing to partake in bloodshed profanely
questions.explanation: Verse 19 shows David’s sanctified attitude, refusing to treat the costly sacrifice lightly, reflecting holiness and reverence.

questions.question: How do verses 26-47 contribute to the biblical theology of faithful service and divine gifting in the community of God’s people?
options: They list many valiant men, illustrating God’s gifting diverse individuals for His purposes
They focus only on David and ignore others
They emphasize human strength apart from God
questions.correctAnswer: They list many valiant men, illustrating God’s gifting diverse individuals for His purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 26-47 name many warriors, showing God’s providential gifting of various people to serve His kingdom.

questions.question: What synthesis of divine kingship and human responsibility is taught by combining 1 Chronicles 11:2 and 1 Chronicles 11:25 regarding David’s role and his guard?
options: God appoints rulers, who in turn appoint faithful stewards to maintain order under divine authority
David ruled without any human helpers
David ignored his guard and responsibilities
questions.correctAnswer: God appoints rulers, who in turn appoint faithful stewards to maintain order under divine authority
questions.explanation: Verse 2 shows God’s appointment of David, and verse 25 shows David appointing Benaiah over the guard, reflecting shared divine-human governance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine deliverance and human faithfulness is taught by 1 Chronicles 11:13-14 and 1 Chronicles 11:18-19?
options: God delivers His people in battle when they act faithfully and honor sacrifices
Victory comes without reliance on God
Sacrifices are irrelevant to God's intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers His people in battle when they act faithfully and honor sacrifices
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 recount God’s deliverance in battle, and verses 18-19 show honoring sacrifice, linking faithfulness with divine deliverance.
